documents.title: Done with chemo
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Sixth and last round of chemo was yesterday!! Now it's just the Herceptin every 3 weeks, and radiation starts mid February. I'd like to come in sometime in February if you have time, nothing urgent.

documents.title: RE: Done with chemo
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Congratulations! You're booked Thursday 2/13 at 4:00 with the doctor.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Finished 6 cycles of TCH 1/16. Continuing trastuzumab q3wk. Radiation to R breast/axilla starts Monday, about 6 weeks. Energy coming back slowly. Hair growing in.
Neck and L arm: no pain or tingling for over a month. Finished PT, does the exercises at home and changed how she sits at the chair at work.
Hot flashes several times a day, worse at night with sweats. No period since October. Oncology aware.
Neurology letter received in December - reviewed.

O: Vitals as charted, BP at goal. Neck full ROM, no pain. Arm strength and sensation normal to light touch, reflexes symmetric. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P
1. Cervical radiculopathy - resolved with PT. Off problem list.
2. Breast ca on trastuzumab, radiation next; tamoxifen to follow per oncology.
3. Vasomotor symptoms with chemo-related loss of periods - bothersome. She'd like to see a gynecologist about it once radiation is done; she will call the one her friends use.
4. HTN controlled. BMP today.
5. Lipids - recheck at physical in the fall.

documents.title: Radiation finished
documents.author: patient
documents.body: FYI finished radiation Friday. Skin is pink and sore under my arm but settling. Oncology is starting me on tamoxifen next week. Still getting Herceptin.

documents.title: RE: Radiation finished
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great news to finish. Thanks for the update - I'll add tamoxifen to your list once you start.

documents.body: Pharmacy fill history shows tamoxifen 20 mg tablets, #30, filled 4/7/2025, prescriber outside oncology. Added to med list as outside prescription.

documents.title: Gynecology Consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outside gynecology office - visit 6/10/2025.

47-year-old seen for hot flashes and night sweats over roughly half a year that wake her most nights and are wearing on her at work. Background: right breast cancer (HER2+, hormone receptor+) treated with lumpectomy, chemotherapy and radiation; currently on trastuzumab infusions and tamoxifen. No menses since chemotherapy last autumn. Hypertension on hydrochlorothiazide and lisinopril. NKDA. Non-smoker, no alcohol.

BP 128/78, HR 76, BMI 26. General exam unremarkable.

Labs: FSH 82 IU/L and estradiol <20 pg/mL, both in the postmenopausal range. CBC and liver tests normal.

Assessment: menopausal vasomotor syndrome after chemotherapy-induced ovarian suppression, aggravated by tamoxifen. Hormone therapy is not an option with her cancer.

Plan: layered clothing, cooler bedroom, sleep routine, avoid known triggers. Offered venlafaxine as a non-hormonal option compatible with tamoxifen; she prefers to hold off for now. Return in 6 months or sooner with bleeding.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: eRx renewal request hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg and lisinopril 10 mg, 90-day supply. Last BMP 2/2025 normal. Approved per protocol x1; physical due in the fall - reminder sent.

conditions.label: Cardiomyopathy due to drug and external agent
conditions.note: trastuzumab-induced cardiotoxicity, asymptomatic left ventricular dysfunction, LVEF 45% from 55%

medications.reason: LVEF decline; 16 of 17 planned doses given

documents.title: Medical Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside medical oncology - follow-up 9/8/2025.

Right breast IDC, pT2 pN0, ER+/PR+/HER2+. Chemotherapy and radiation finished about six months ago; trastuzumab alone every 3 weeks since. Tamoxifen 20 mg daily since April. She has no shortness of breath, chest pain or palpitations.

BP 130/85, HR 78. Examination unremarkable, no edema, lungs clear.

Surveillance echocardiogram today: LVEF 45%. Pre-treatment echocardiogram (9/2024): LVEF 55%.

Assessment: asymptomatic left ventricular dysfunction due to trastuzumab, a 10-point fall to below 50%.

Plan: trastuzumab held today. She has received 16 of 17 planned doses; after discussion we will not resume it. Continue lisinopril. Repeat echocardiogram in 3 months. Continue tamoxifen. Next oncology visit in 3 months.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
48F, annual. Missed last year's physical during treatment.

Interval: oncology letter 9/15 received - LVEF 45% from 55% on trastuzumab, no symptoms; trastuzumab stopped for good, repeat echo in December. Tamoxifen since April. Gyn saw her in June for hot flashes, labs postmenopausal range; she declined venlafaxine.
Feels well, no exertional dyspnea, orthopnea or swelling. Hot flashes still there but she's coping. Weight up about 4 kg since spring - less active, snacking at night when she can't sleep.
PHQ-2 1.

Exam: vitals as charted. R breast healed lumpectomy scar, radiation skin changes mild; no masses either breast, no axillary nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur or gallop, no JVD. Lungs clear. No edema. Neck full ROM.

A/P
1. Trastuzumab-related LV dysfunction, asymptomatic - trastuzumab removed from med list. Lisinopril continues (also helps here). Repeat echo per oncology.
2. Breast ca on tamoxifen; surveillance mammogram due ~1 yr after surgery/radiation - oncology arranging.
3. HTN controlled. CMP.
4. Lipids, CBC, TSH today.
5. Weight gain - talked about evening routine and walking again.
6. Flu + updated COVID today.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your labs are back: kidney and liver tests, potassium, blood counts and thyroid are normal. Cholesterol is about where it was last year. Good to see your blood counts fully recovered after chemo.

documents.title: Oncology note - repeat echocardiogram
documents.author: oncology
documents.body: Outside medical oncology, brief note. Repeat transthoracic echocardiogram 12/10/2025: LVEF 50%, improved from 45% in September. Remains asymptomatic. Trastuzumab remains discontinued. Continue lisinopril and tamoxifen. Surveillance mammogram ordered for January. Next visit in 4 months.

conditions.label: Benign endometrial hyperplasia
conditions.note: hyperplasia without atypia on office biopsy, on tamoxifen

reports.text: Transabdominal and transvaginal pelvic ultrasound. Uterus anteverted, mildly enlarged, homogeneous myometrium. Endometrium measures 14 mm, without focal lesion on grayscale. Both ovaries visualized, normal in size and appearance. No adnexal mass. No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Thickened endometrium, 14 mm, in a patient on tamoxifen. Normal ovaries, no adnexal mass.

reports.text: Specimen: endometrium, office pipelle biopsy. Fragments of proliferative-type endometrium with an increased gland-to-stroma ratio and glandular crowding; glands with cytologic features matching the background endometrium. No cytologic atypia. No carcinoma.

documents.title: Gynecology Visit
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outside gynecology office - visit 12/24/2025.

Returns for routine follow-up; seen in June for vasomotor symptoms on tamoxifen. Two months of irregular bleeding - unpredictable spotting and light flow after more than a year without periods. Hot flashes and night sweats continue. Tamoxifen about 8 months.

Meds per patient list: hydrochlorothiazide, lisinopril, tamoxifen, trastuzumab. NKDA.

BP 130/85, BMI 29.
Pelvic exam: uterus slightly enlarged, non-tender. No adnexal masses.

Labs: hemoglobin 13.2 g/dL, platelets 250,000, PT 11 s, aPTT 30 s.
Pelvic ultrasound today: endometrium 14 mm, no adnexal mass.
Office endometrial biopsy performed today; result 12/30: endometrial hyperplasia without atypia.

Assessment: endometrial hyperplasia without atypia, on tamoxifen; irregular bleeding as ovarian function returns after chemotherapy.

Plan: levonorgestrel intrauterine system recommended, placement scheduled 1/14. Discussed with her oncologist: continue tamoxifen. Repeat endometrial sampling in 3 to 6 months.
